args.reason: The PRDR serves the first PRD goal and stays inside it. All three DoD items are about inspecting the current merge decision without merging: exit 0 with merge-ok, exit 1 with the blocked conditions, and a test double proving gh pr merge is never called. Nothing in the DoD stores or queries history, which the PRD puts out of scope. The second goal holds because the dry run reuses the existing floor reads rather than adding a separate eligibility path. One point to check at build time: the dry-run path must call the same floor function as the real merge, not a copy, or the second goal would quietly break.
